doc.title: Terms
doc.para: Terms Terms have the highest precedence in expression evaluation. In addition to ordinary immediate values and identifiers , these include the following:

true and false true and false ( true and false ) are treated as integer values with the values 1 and 0, respectively.
Please avoid comparing other expressions with true or false. For example, do not do something like if(true != getBoolean()), but write if(!getBoolen()) instead. This is because in logical expressions, "0 is false" and "non-zero is true", rather than "1 is true", and TJS2 does not have a Boolean type, so automatic conversions between numeric and Boolean types are not performed.

void void indicates "nothing". It is used in various situations to represent "nothing". It is different from null. Newly declared variables (variables to which nothing has been assigned) have this value. When treated as a string, it becomes an empty string ( '' ). When treated as a number, it becomes 0.
We recommend using the === or !== (identity) operator when comparing void values with each other.

null null indicates an object, but one that "points to no object". It is different from void. Attempting to access a null object will result in an error. If you change the context to null using the incontextof operator, the function will execute in the context of the location where it was called.
var objmethod = obj.method; objmethod(); // Executed in the context of obj objmethod = objmethod incontextof null; // Change context to null objmethod(); // Executed on this (that is, the context at the calling location)
Infinity Infinity represents infinity. To represent negative infinity, use -Infinity.
NaN NaN represents NaN (Not a Number). Non-numbers are numeric values obtained when the result of a calculation is invalid, etc.

super super represents the superclass of a class inside that class's methods or properties. Attempting to reference it outside of a class method/property, or within a class using multiple inheritance, will result in an error.
this this usually represents the object itself of a class inside that class's methods or properties. The "context" specified explicitly or implicitly at the time of invocation is specified as this.
